title: Conditional aggregation: SUMIFS, COUNTIFS and AVERAGEIFS

videos.script: Lesson one ended on a report. Products down the side, months across the top, bags in every cell. {{report}} Somebody built it by hand. Filter the channel, select the column, read the total, type it in. Next month, they do it again. {{filter}} This lesson writes that question down as a formula. SUMIFS adds the rows that pass every condition you give it. COUNTIFS counts them. AVERAGEIFS averages them. {{three}} All three read the sheet one row at a time. Is the channel Wholesale? Is the product the one kilo Cerrado? A row that passes every test is used. A row that fails one test is skipped. {{rows}} A condition can be more than equal to. Ten bags or more. Any product ending in two fifty. Every sale from the first of January. {{criteria}} And a condition can point at a cell. So one formula, copied across and down, fills a whole grid, and the report from lesson one rebuilds itself. {{grid}} Last, the habit that makes all of it trustworthy. The three channels must add up to the total. When they do not, a condition is wrong, and now there is a formula to read. {{check}}
